compatibility_regressions: The contract intentionally changes un-IDed string output from [foo] and [bar] to ['foo'] and ['bar'].
Preserving explicit IDs literally diverges from the hindsight implementation, which applies saferepr to every cached parameter at display time and therefore quotes string IDs.
invented_requirements: Cache the safe representation at fixture setup time instead of applying saferepr at the shared display site.
Preserve explicit list-based and callable string IDs without saferepr; the sealed MD1 owner answer called for safe bounded representation consistently, including the user-visible custom-ID surface.
Require the bytes regression to run under all three setup-display modes; this was interview-confirmed but exceeds the reported --setup-show case and hindsight regression construction.
redundant_questions: The explicit-ID question reopened a behavior already covered by MD1's sealed owner answer favoring consistent safe representation.
The test-scope and warning-mechanism questions selected test-construction details beyond the single material product decision.
summary: The contract is implementable and accurately identifies the unsafe implicit string conversion, shared setup/teardown display path, saferepr utility, bytes representation, and intentional quoting of ordinary strings. It fully resolves its own stated decisions, but it departs from the sealed MD1 answer and hindsight implementation by exempting explicit IDs from saferepr and by prescribing caching the representation rather than formatting at the shared display site. Hindsight-only details such as maxsize=42 and sys.executable -bb were appropriately not treated as owner requirements.
